items.prompt: In a B-tree of order 4, how many children can an internal node other than the root have?
hints: The order is the most children a node may have.
An internal node other than the root has at least ⌈m/2⌉ children.
⌈4/2⌉ = 2, so 2 to 4 children.

options.feedback: Right: at least ⌈4/2⌉ = 2 and at most 4.
4 is the maximum. A node may be anything from half full to full.
An internal node with one child would hold no keys. The minimum is ⌈m/2⌉ = 2.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-3 B-tree?
hints: Count the root's keys and children.
A node with k keys that is not a leaf has k + 1 children.
The root has 2 keys but only 2 children. It needs 3.

items.prompt: Tap the nodes a search for 30 visits, from the root down.
hints: Start at the root.
At each node, follow the child for 30's range.

items.prompt: You insert 25 into this order-4 B-tree. What happens?
hints: Which leaf does 25 belong in?
An order-4 node holds up to 3 keys.
25 < 30 → left leaf [10 | 20], which has room: it becomes [10 | 20 | 25].

options.text: The left leaf becomes [10 | 20 | 25], with no split
options.feedback: Right. An order-4 leaf holds up to 3 keys, so 25 fits.

options.text: The left leaf splits and 20 moves up
options.feedback: A node only splits when it has more than m − 1 = 3 keys.
New keys always go into a leaf.

items.prompt: You insert 30 into this order-3 B-tree. Which key moves up to the parent?
hints: Put 30 into the leaf first.
The leaf now holds 3 keys, so it splits around its middle key.
The leaf becomes [20, 30, 40]. The middle key is 30, the key you just inserted, so 30 moves up.

items.prompt: You insert 55 into this order-3 B-tree. Which key ends up as the new root?
hints: Which leaf gets 55, and does it overflow?
When the key that moves up overflows the root, the root splits too.
[50 | 55 | 60] splits and 55 moves up. The root [20 | 40 | 55] splits and 40 becomes the new root.

options.feedback: Right. The split reaches the root, and the root's middle key becomes a new root.
55 moves up into the root, but then the root holds [20 | 40 | 55] and its middle key, 40, moves up.

options.text: There is no new root: the root just becomes [20 | 40 | 55]
options.feedback: An order-3 root holds at most 2 keys, so it must split.

items.prompt: A B-tree of order 200 holds 1 000 000 keys. About how many levels does it have?
hints: Each level multiplies the number of nodes by up to 200.
Even half-full nodes have at least 100 children.

options.feedback: Right. That is about 3 disk reads to find any key.
That is the height of a balanced binary tree.
The height grows logarithmically, not linearly.

items.prompt: You delete 30 from this order-3 B-tree. What is in the root afterwards?
hints: Removing 30 empties its leaf. Look at both siblings.
The left sibling [10] has only the minimum. The right sibling [50 | 60] can spare a key.
Borrow from the right: 40 comes down, 50 goes up. The root becomes [20 | 50].

options.feedback: Right. The right sibling spares 50 through the parent, and 40 comes down.
Merging is only needed when no sibling can spare a key. [50 | 60] can.
The empty leaf would break the minimum-keys rule. The underflow has to be fixed.
